title: A practitioner's dispensing to an ultimate user is limited to what immediate and proper treatment requires
subtopic: Dispensing by delivering to an ultimate user
rule_summary: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 9(b) provides that, notwithstanding section 17, a physician, physician assistant, dentist, podiatrist, optometrist, certified nurse midwife, licensed certified professional midwife, nurse practitioner, psychiatric nurse mental health clinical specialist, nurse anesthetist, pharmacist as limited by s. 7(g) and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2, or veterinarian registered under s. 7 may, when acting in good faith and in the practice of the profession concerned, dispense by delivering to an ultimate user a controlled substance in a single dose or in a quantity that is, in the practitioner's opinion, essential for the treatment of a patient. The amount or quantity of any controlled substance dispensed under the subsection shall not exceed the quantity of a controlled substance necessary for the immediate and proper treatment of the patient until it is possible for the patient to have a prescription filled by a pharmacy. All controlled substances required by the patient as part of the patient's treatment shall be dispensed by prescription to the ultimate user in accordance with chapter 94C. The section does not prohibit or limit the dispensing of a prescription medication classified by the department as Schedule VI and provided by the manufacturer as part of an indigent patient program or for use as samples if it is dispensed to the patient by a professional authorized to dispense controlled substances under the section, dispensed in the package provided by the manufacturer, and provided at no charge to the patient. The department shall promulgate rules and regulations governing the dispensing of medication under the section, which shall include, but not be limited to, the types and amounts of medications that may be dispensed and the appropriate safeguards for their labeling and dispensing.
exam_relevance: Tests that a Massachusetts practitioner's own dispensing to a patient is capped at the quantity necessary for immediate and proper treatment until a prescription can be filled by a pharmacy, that controlled substances needed for ongoing treatment are to be dispensed by prescription, and that the department regulates the types and amounts a practitioner may dispense.
exceptions: The section does not prohibit or limit the dispensing of a Schedule VI prescription medication provided by the manufacturer as part of an indigent patient program or for use as samples, if it is dispensed to the patient by a professional authorized to dispense controlled substances under the section, in the package provided by the manufacturer, and at no charge to the patient.
common_confusions: Treating a practitioner's dispensing to a patient as open-ended, when the quantity may not exceed what is necessary for immediate and proper treatment until a prescription can be filled by a pharmacy.
Overlooking that controlled substances required as part of the patient's treatment are to be dispensed by prescription.
verification_notes: Read in the current text of M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 9 on malegislature.gov on 2026-09-16.
